lede:
The easiest set in the game to keep apart, and the exact opposite of the brace problem: sixteen names that are already sixteen different objects. Dross, a hairline crack, a coolant plume, a scored bore, a blown coupling, a dead cell, a loose round, an arc fault, a torn liner, a fouled optic, ballast, a jammed feed, a slow fire, a ghost return, slag, a seized actuator.

What the keywords mean, and how they show

Every malfunction has Purge and most carry Corrode (rust, pitting, bloom), Smoulder (heat, smoke, char) or Fused (stuck, cannot be discarded). So the keyword drives the damage and the name drives the object — which is why no two of these should look alike even though all sixteen mean 'something on your ship is wrong'.

They are all close details of a bigger machine, which is a frame no card in the game uses yet: the weapon cards are wide exteriors and the two instrument cards are flat faces. That separation is deliberate — a hand of malfunctions should feel different from a hand of attacks before you read a word of it.

These are also the only cards a player never chooses. They arrive as punishment, so the pictures should be unwelcome: cold, still, already broken, nothing dramatic happening. Damage already done, not an explosion in progress.

cards.actor: the slag skimmed off a smelt
cards.on: the crusted grey scab it has left welded to a deck plate
cards.moment: a cooled tongue of waste metal fused where it ran, dull and porous, nobody's job to remove.
cards.scale: a hand-sized detail of a much larger machine: bolt heads, weld seams and stencilled lettering give the size without anything else in frame.
cards.world: in the void or on the outside of something in it -- never an interior room. Dithered indigo ground with a rusty amber nebula wash, everything coldly lit, the only warm light self-emitted. Weathered plating with stencils and decals.
cards.avoid: an interior room with a floor. No figures. Never say gun, weapon, cannon, barrel, hull, vessel, shell, starship or flank. A malfunction is DAMAGE ALREADY DONE, not an explosion happening.
